reconcile.connective: Defenders read the shorter lists as selective, not contradictory: each evangelist names the women that suited his account, none claiming a complete tally.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman presses that the Gospels cannot agree on who went to the tomb — one woman, two, three, or more — and that no two lists of names match.

excerpts.author: Adam Clarke
excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: John only mentions Mary of Magdala, because he appears to wish to give a more detailed history of her conduct than of any of the rest; but the other evangelists speak of three persons who went together to the tomb, viz. Mary of Magdala, Mary the mother of James, and Salome: Mat 28:1; Mar 16:1.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the count tension: John names only Mary Magdalene because his interest is in her, while the other evangelists report multiple women — selective focus, not conflicting numbers.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats the differing resurrection-morning witness lists directly, arguing each evangelist records a partial, selective roster rather than an exhaustive count of the women.

link.title: GotQuestions: Can the various resurrection accounts from the four Gospels be harmonized?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment arguing no Gospel claims a complete list (Luke names 'other women'), so the differing numbers are selective, not contradictory.
